summary.headline: Centum's standalone FY26 revenue rose 25% to a record INR 973 crores, while overseas exits drove a INR 203 crore exceptional charge.
summary.overview: Standalone Q4 FY26 revenue was INR 344 crores (+26% YoY) with EBITDA margin of 13.22%, and FY26 standalone EBITDA was INR 121 crores (12.42% margin), below the 13-15% target range. Consolidated FY26 revenue was INR 953 crores (+29%) with PAT from continuing operations of INR 101 crores, doubling YoY. Canada was discontinued and the French subsidiary entered court-supervised restructuring in March 2026, with both now classified as discontinued operations and assets held for sale. Management said the standalone order book closed at about INR 1,645 crores (+23%) and expects deconsolidation of the French entity around Q1 or early Q2 FY27.

segments.name: Build-to-Specification (BTS, standalone)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue grew about 37% YoY, driven by space payloads, radar subsystems, and land and missile subsystems. Around INR 400 crores of orders booked in FY26 against about INR 250 crores of BTS revenue; BTS EBITDA margin is around 20%.

segments.name: Electronics Manufacturing Services (EMS)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue grew about 21% YoY on semiconductor equipment ramp-ups and new wins in industrial, electrification, grid automation and defence exports. EMS margins run about 9-10% on a cost-plus basis, with occasional peaks near 11%.

guidance_outlook: Medium-term standalone growth target of 25-30% CAGR, with management declining to give year-on-year guidance.
EBITDA margin target of 13-15% at combined level, expected to be reached over the next 1-2 years and sustained for 2-3 years.
FY27 capex of about INR 40-45 crores, roughly half or slightly more for BTS R&D capabilities.

European subsidiary court process expected to conclude around June/July 2026; management expects no realisation and no further exceptional items from it in FY27, given liabilities exceed assets by over INR 100 crores.
Deconsolidation of the French subsidiary possibly at end of Q1 FY27, worst case Q2; Q1 losses expected to be similar to or lower than recent run-rate.
Management expects to book the roughly INR 100-150 crores of spillover BTS orders in Q1 or Q2 FY27, and BTS order book entering FY27 at about INR 800 crores.
capex_capacity: FY27 capex planned at about INR 40-45 crores, with BTS R&D capability as the larger component.
Investments continue in additional manufacturing lines, process automation and systems integration capabilities for EMS.
Standalone order book closed FY26 at about INR 1,645 crores (+23% YoY); order book grew about 2.3x over three years for BTS (32% CAGR) and about 1.7x at entity level (20% CAGR).
UHM AESA radar order from HAL worth over INR 570 crores over life cycle: about INR 67 crores development phase over 2 years, then about INR 500 crores-plus execution through FY30-FY31.
demand_pricing: Defence and aerospace is addressed by both BTS and EMS; BTS is almost entirely defence and space, with customers mainly HAL, DRDO and BEL.

Semiconductor equipment EMS growth is driven by one anchor customer; discussions with a couple of other customers are at a preliminary stage. Management referenced a USD 30 million revenue question without committing to a target.

Virupaksha radar: two development subsystem orders (antenna array and exciter-receiver) worth under INR 10 crores. Space debris tracking long-range radar order is about INR 30-odd crores for one system, also a development order.

Supply chain: copper clad laminate and memory component lead times have lengthened, linked partly to AI data centre demand. Management is placing orders earlier to secure supply, and said supply continues to meet requirements.
Middle East war caused short-term logistics delays at end of Q4 FY26; no major supply disruption seen so far.

qa_highlights.question: Why was full-year margin about 12.5%, below the 13-15% guided range, despite higher BTS share?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the shortfall to EMS product mix, which was below initial expectations; some of that mix is expected to be executed in FY27, supporting better EMS margins.

qa_highlights.question: Will the European sale bring any cash realisation?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Management said no realisation is expected, and the balance sheet carries liabilities held for disposal well above assets, with a net excess over INR 100 crores.

qa_highlights.question: Did FY26 standalone BTS order inflow grow only about 4%?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said about INR 470 crores was booked and reported; the figure was recast to exclude subsidiary contributions. Around INR 100-150 crores slipped into FY27, and a significant FY27 order growth is expected.

qa_highlights.question: What is the scope and timeline for the INR 570 crore UHM radar order?
qa_highlights.answer: The scope is a full turnkey radar delivered to HAL, covering development, qualification and airborne certification. The development phase is about 2 years, with the remaining execution through FY30-FY31.

qa_highlights.question: What is the tax position on losses from the standalone exceptional items?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said INR 153 crores of the INR 200 crore standalone exceptional items is an investment impairment, treated as a capital loss available to offset future capital gains. The remaining items were offset against FY26 profits. Subsidiary tax credits are not expected to be realised.

qa_highlights.question: How much loss should be expected from discontinued operations in Q1 FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: No precise forecast was given. Management said the figure could be similar to the recent run-rate, with some acceleration from slower French revenue in May, but Q4's INR 33 crore discontinued loss included Canada and one-offs and should not be used as a guide.

risks_watch: Timing of the French court-supervised asset sale and whether deconsolidation happens in Q1 or Q2 FY27.
Standalone EBITDA margin of 12.42% in FY26 was below the 13-15% target; delivery of the EMS mix improvement is pending.
Lengthening lead times for copper clad laminate and memory components could affect EMS delivery.
Conversion of BTS spillover orders of INR 100-150 crores into Q1-Q2 FY27 and the pace of the HAL UHM order's execution.
Possible competition with HAL, BEL and DRDO customers as the company moves up the value chain into system-level work.
Concentration risk: semiconductor equipment growth relies mainly on one anchor customer.
summary.management_tone: Confident on standalone growth, order book and medium-term targets, but cautious and non-committal on quarterly guidance and on the timing of the European deconsolidation. Management repeatedly redirected analysts from consolidated numbers to standalone figures.
key_quotes: We closed the year with a standalone order book of approximately INR 1,645 crores, representing a growth of around 23% year-on-year and providing strong visibility for the coming years.

And really consolidated numbers don't really mean much from a P&L standpoint anymore. It should really be focused on standalone.

growth.why: Management targets a 25-30% medium-term standalone CAGR (declining YoY guidance) backed by a standalone order book of about INR 1,645 crores (+23%), including ~INR 800 crores of BTS orders entering FY27 and INR 100-150 crores of spillover expected in Q1-Q2 FY27, though no new capacity beyond FY27 capex of INR 40-45 crores is quantified.
